parts.ask: A student is asked: given that \(x\) is an obtuse angle, use algebra to prove by contradiction that \(\sin x - \cos x \geq 1\). The student starts: assume that \(\sin x - \cos x < 1\) when \(x\) is obtuse, so \((\sin x - \cos x)^2 < 1\). Complete the proof.

steps.text: Assume that \(\sin x - \cos x < 1\) when \(x\) is obtuse.

steps.why: Squaring is safe: for obtuse \(x\), \(\sin x - \cos x > 0\).

steps.tex: (\sin x - \cos x)^2 = \sin^2 x - 2\sin x\cos x + \cos^2 x

steps.head: Now look at the signs for obtuse \(x\)

steps.text: So \(-2\sin x\cos x\) is \((-) \times (+) \times (-)\), which is positive: \(-2\sin x\cos x > 0\).

steps.why: Name the contradiction and say why: signs in the second quadrant.

parts.answerText: So the assumption is false: if \(x\) is obtuse, then \(\sin x - \cos x \geq 1\).

check.answers: proof by contradiction: the assert checks (sin x - cos x)^2 = 1 - 2 sin x cos x, and that -2 sin x cos x > 0 and sin x - cos x >= 1 at every whole degree from 91 to 179
check.assert: simplify((sin(x) - cos(x))**2 - (1 - 2*sin(x)*cos(x))) == 0 and all((-2*sin(rad(a))*cos(rad(a))).evalf() > 0 and (sin(rad(a)) - cos(rad(a))).evalf() >= 1 for a in range(91, 180))
